title: Relative citations (tok mode 'rel') instead of absolute line indices
description: The fork's tokenizer has a 'rel' mode: line numbers are dropped and a citation becomes B<k> = k lines back, decoded deterministically. Same model and optimizer as 001.
hypothesis: Absolute indices N1..N64 tie the model to line positions seen in cap-6 data (with random-shift augmentation as a patch). Relative references are position-free, so a 7-9 line proof is made of the same local patterns as a 6-line one. This is the kind of structural change that could move transfer beyond the noise. Risk: Dan chose abs for a reason in later runs.
surprise: Loss 0.009 vs 0.064 (no shift augmentation noise in rel mode) and greedy 0.945, yet EI round 1 solved only 42 targets vs 76: the rel model samples less usefully at T=0.8 beyond cap 6. Looks like a real negative, not just noise, since r1 solved is the most stable intermediate stat so far (76, 76, 85, 30, 42).
